_meta.description: Portfolio summary — the synthesizing view: the defining insight, thematic clusters, a four-question framework for any position, and a catalyst calendar by vertical.

defining_insight.title: Own the chokepoints; the bottleneck owners win regardless of which brand wins
defining_insight.body: Across this entire universe, value concentrates at the stages no one can easily replicate: ASML (EUV), TSMC (leading-edge + CoWoS), SK Hynix (HBM), Nvidia/Broadcom (platform + ASIC), plus the quiet upstream Japanese chokepoints (wafers, resist, reducers). The end-products — GPUs vs ASICs, this robot vs that, one glasses brand vs another — are contested and crowded, but they all flow through the same narrow gates. The most durable exposure is upstream at the bottleneck, not downstream at the brand. The dominant structural risk overlaying all of it is the geographic concentration in Taiwan + Korea.

clusters.title: Asia proxies
items: Foxconn / Quanta / Wiwynn — AI server ODM

four_questions.a: Is this a stage only a handful of players can do (ASML, TSMC CoWoS, HBM, reducers) — or a contested, capacity-adds-easily layer (OSAT overflow, transceiver assembly, robot brands)? Pay up for the former; trade the latter on the cycle.

four_questions.q: Who captures value vs who does volume?
four_questions.a: Volume and value often sit in different places: China assembles ~63% of transceivers but US silicon + lasers capture the margin; ASICs may take share but TSMC + HBM win either way. Buy the value-capture layer, not the volume layer.

How concentrated in Taiwan/Korea is it, and is it an export-control target or lever (EDA, WFE, HBM, China stack)? Concentration is both the moat and the tail risk — size accordingly and watch policy on/off switches.

Does demand persist through a hyperscaler capex pause (EDA royalties, mature-node) or does it hinge entirely on AI capex ROI continuing (accelerators, networking, power/cooling)? Match position size to where you sit on that spectrum.

cats.t: TSMC Q3 report — does capex fear break?
cats.p: TSMC raised its 2026 build budget to $60–64B and the stock FELL. The next quarterly report shows whether the market goes back to reading big capex as strong demand.
cats.why: The best sentiment gauge for the whole AI supply chain — and the catalyst on our #1 entry window.

cats.t: N2 (2-nanometer) volume ramp, A16 behind it
cats.p: TSMC's newest manufacturing generation is filling with orders through 2026; the next one (A16) is already being sold.
cats.why: Confirms the leading edge stays sold out — the core of the TSM thesis.

cats.p: New packaging plants to relieve the #1 AI bottleneck — ~1M wafers of 2026 demand already booked, Nvidia holding ~60%.
cats.why: More CoWoS = more AI chips can physically ship; watch who catches the overflow (ASE, Amkor).

cats.p: The next escape from round-wafer size limits: building chip packages on large rectangular panels instead.
cats.why: Would reshuffle the packaging-equipment winners.

cats.t: HBM4 qualified by all three makers
cats.p: For the first time in HBM's history, SK Hynix, Samsung AND Micron all passed qualification for the same generation — and all ship for Vera Rubin.
cats.why: Confirms structural demand — but three qualified suppliers also means more supply. Watch pricing.

cats.t: SK Hynix Q3: delayed HBM4 revenue lands
cats.p: The HBM4 shipments that slipped out of Q2 get recognized in the September quarter — the print that answers July's air-pocket selloff.
cats.why: The catalyst on our #2 entry window: confirms or breaks the 'repriced, not broken' read.

cats.t: Samsung share recovery vs SK Hynix
cats.p: Samsung fell badly behind in AI memory; it is now qualified and shipping an estimated 25–30% of Nvidia's newest platform.
cats.why: Drives the Samsung re-rating ('Korea Unlocked') thesis.

cats.p: China's memory champion trying to build HBM without Western tools.
cats.why: The long-term supply and geopolitics wildcard for memory pricing.

cats.p: Nvidia's next flagship platform is in full production and ships in Q3 — each GPU carries 288GB of HBM4 across eight stacks.
cats.why: Resets the content story downstream: more memory, more optics, more power per chip.

cats.p: The big AI labs increasingly co-design their own chips with Broadcom or Marvell instead of buying only Nvidia — OpenAI signed ~$10B with Broadcom starting late 2026.
cats.why: Confirms the custom-silicon thesis: value shifts to the ASIC partners and the network.

cats.p: The five biggest US cloud builders plan ~$700B of 2026 investment — revised UP $173B since January. Every earnings season re-tests it.
cats.why: The demand spine under every name in this dashboard. Never stop watching this number.

cats.p: As AI moves from building models to running them everywhere, cheaper inference silicon takes a growing share of spend — inference prices are already down 30–40% this year.
cats.why: Decides how durable Nvidia's premium is, and which GPU renters survive.

cats.p: Optics built directly into the switch — Nvidia on TSMC's COUPE process, Broadcom's Bailly — started shipping in real volume. No longer a roadmap item.
cats.why: Confirms the optics content story; the bottleneck moved to optical-engine yield — good for COHR, LITE, FOCI.

cats.p: The next speed grade of plug-in optics ramping through 2026.
cats.why: Content per GPU keeps climbing — the core optics thesis.

cats.t: EML laser capacity — does the shortage ease?
cats.p: The tiny lasers at the heart of every optical module remain the chokepoint; capacity comes on slowly.
cats.why: Tight lasers mean pricing power for the few makers; a real easing would soften it.

cats.t: LPO/CPO reshuffle of the value chain
cats.p: As optics integrate into the chip package, today's module assemblers risk losing their seat at the table.
cats.why: Decides who captures optics value in 2028+ — component owners over assemblers.

cats.p: New AI racks increasingly REQUIRE water cooling; attach rises with every GPU generation.
cats.why: Drives Vertiv, AVC, Auras — cooling grows faster than the market it serves.

cats.p: Racks are being redesigned around 800V DC power (borrowed from the EV industry) for Nvidia's next platforms; first real shipments expected imminently.
cats.why: Opens the SiC/GaN power-chip story: Infineon, onsemi, Navitas, Delta, Lite-On.

cats.t: Grid equipment lead times stay multi-year
cats.p: Transformers and switchgear still quote waits measured in years.
cats.why: The physical ceiling on AI growth — supports Hitachi Energy, Siemens Energy, GE Vernova.

cats.p: Datacenters signing direct contracts with power plants next door instead of waiting years for grid hookups.
cats.why: Turns the AI-power story from narrative into contracted cash flow — the CEG/VST layer.

cats.p: Tesla's robot line is live — roughly 100–150/week in July, targeting 1,000/week by September, all for internal use first.
cats.why: The volume signal the whole actuator chain has been waiting for.

cats.p: The component makers (precision gears, screws) began receiving real purchase orders, not just samples — supplier stocks surged Jul 10.
cats.why: Confirms the T-chain thesis (Tuopu, Shuanghuan, Beite). Now watch order sizes against the stock moves.

cats.t: Unitree IPO prices on the STAR board
cats.p: China's leading robot maker goes public (~$619M raise filed) — and its filing revealed profits HALVED.
cats.why: The first real public-market test of humanoid-maker economics.

cats.p: Chinese suppliers driving joint costs down fast enough to make robots economical.
cats.why: Decides where actuator value settles — Japanese quality vs Chinese price.

cats.p: Can anyone build a genuinely useful humanoid below ~$30–50K at real scale?
cats.why: The make-or-break question for the size of the entire theme.

cats.p: The first mainstream glasses with a built-in display — do people keep buying them after the novelty?
cats.why: The consumer on-ramp for the whole AR component chain.

cats.p: Google's glasses platform brings more hardware brands to market.
cats.why: More devices = more volume for displays, waveguides and the Qualcomm SoC layer.

cats.p: MicroLED vs OLED-on-silicon vs LCoS — still no winner for true AR glasses.
cats.why: Picks the winners in the display vertical; several leaders are still private.

cats.t: High-NA EUV used in real production
cats.p: ASML's newest ~$380M machines are now running actual manufacturing at Intel (the 18A process) — not just development work.
cats.why: Validates the next decade of ASML's roadmap; watch TSMC and Samsung follow.

cats.p: Chinese fabs over-ordered equipment for years; that hangover is fading just as AI fab construction accelerates.
cats.why: Sets up the cycle turn for AMAT, Lam, TEL, KLA.

cats.p: US rules on selling chip-design software to China keep changing with the political weather.
cats.why: The main risk overhang on Synopsys/Cadence multiples.

cats.p: China replacing Western fab tools wherever it can (NAURA, AMEC) — lithography excepted.
cats.why: Long-term share risk in mid-tier tools; ASML's moat stays intact.

cats.t: China rare-earth truce: renew or lapse (Nov 10)
cats.p: The Oct-2025 escalation of China's rare-earth controls is suspended only until Nov 10, 2026. Renewal keeps the peace; a lapse re-arms the materials weapon overnight.
cats.why: A dated, binary event under the robotics, optics and fab-chemical chains — position sizing should know the date.

cats.p: The H200 was banned, unbanned, then tariffed at 25% within a year; 'green-zone' chips flow while frontier GPUs stay blocked. Another revision is always one announcement away.
cats.why: Swings NVDA/AMD China revenue by billions and re-prices the Chinese domestic-chip cohort in mirror image.

cats.p: Congressional push (Feb 2026) to replace leaky entity-specific equipment controls with a China-wide ban.
cats.why: Would cut the remaining China backlog at AMAT, Lam, KLA and Tokyo Electron — and accelerate NAURA/AMEC substitution.

cats.p: Washington's follow-up debate: extending fab subsidies toward AI datacenters, power and packaging.
cats.why: Decides whether the dci/power build-out gets the same fiscal tailwind fabs got.

cats.p: The June 2026 proposal (demand-side procurement, smaller-country niches) moves through Brussels.
cats.why: Funds the European specialist cohort — ASML, AIXTRON, SUSS, Soitec, AT&S.

entry_windows.intro: Where the July shakeout created price without breaking thesis — conviction-3 chokepoints, insulated on the froth lens, hit by an indiscriminate repricing. A research screen, not advice.

windows.setup: Record Q2 (net profit +77% y/y), RAISED 2026 capex to $60–64B — and the stock fell on capex fear. The keystone of the entire universe repriced on sentiment inversion, not fundamentals.
windows.watch: Q3 print re-anchoring capex-as-demand; CoWoS ~1M wafers already booked with NVDA ~60% locked.
windows.risk: Taiwan concentration; capex-margin fear can run further in a broader drawdown.

windows.setup: Worst Seoul session on record, then a Q2 'miss' at a 76% operating margin — de-rated on LTA contract structure, not demand. Holds an estimated 60–70% of Vera Rubin HBM4 volume.
windows.watch: Full-scale HBM4 revenue recognition in Q3; a concrete shareholder-return plan.
windows.risk: LTAs genuinely cap price upside; a conventional-DRAM glut would sour sentiment further.

windows.setup: Beat on revenue, guided Q3 above consensus, revealed Intel is using high-NA EUV for 18A production — sold off anyway with the complex.
windows.watch: High-NA order momentum now that Intel has validated it in production.
windows.risk: China WFE demand rolling over; order lumpiness always whipsaws the stock.

windows.setup: SOI substrate monopoly still priced for the mobile drag while photonics/POI content inflects — CPO just went volume-production and froth never arrived here.
windows.watch: Photonics-SOI/POI design-win disclosures as COUPE-era optics ramp.
windows.risk: Mobile/auto SOI softness persists longer than the photonics line scales.

windows.setup: The ABF film monopoly inside a food conglomerate — the market still prices seasoning while advanced-packaging substrate capacity is effectively sold out.
windows.watch: ABF capacity expansion tracking the CoWoS/substrate build-out.
windows.risk: The value-unlock discount is perennial; food-business drag on the multiple.

windows.setup: HBM probe-card chokepoint geared to every HBM4 qualification — the first triple-qualified HBM generation means more qual cycles, and the stock sits at a modest multiple.
windows.watch: HBM4 probe-card attach rates through the Q3 Vera Rubin ramp.
windows.risk: A memory-capex digestion phase pauses test spending first.

avoid.title: Where the froth concentrates
avoid.body: The narrative-priced layer, flagged high-froth on the lens: VST (AI-power torque without contracts — CEG is the contracted way), CRWV and NBIS (GPU renters squeezed between 30–40% inference-price deflation and multi-$B lease obligations), ARM (royalty moat priced for decades of share gains), BE (story ahead of margins), SMCI (share-gain story with DELL and HPE closing in). Not shorts — just where a froth unwind lands first.

catalyst_meta.lifecycle: Each catalyst carries status pending/landed/slipped. Landed items stay visible (checked off) for one review cycle before rotating out — a landed catalyst is thesis confirmation, not noise. Reconciling this table against the news is a standing step of every research-loop sweep; if as_of is >60 days old, treat the table as stale.
